statement: If magnitudes be proportional componendo, they will also be proportional separando.
heath_proof: Let AB, BE, CD, DF be magnitudes proportional componendo, so that, as AB is to BE, so is CD to DF; I say that they will also be proportional separando, that is, as AE is to EB, so is CF to DF. For of AE, EB, CF, FD let equimultiples GH, HK, LM, MN be taken, and of EB, FD other, chance, equimultiples, KO, NP. Then, since GH is the same multiple of AE that HK is of EB, therefore GH is the same multiple of AE that GK is of AB. [V. 1] But GH is the same multiple of AE that LM is of CF; therefore GK is the same multiple of AB that LM is of CF. Again, since LM is the same multiple of CF that MN is of FD, therefore LM is the same multiple of CF that LN is of CD. [V. 1] But LM was the same multiple of CF that GK is of AB; therefore GK is the same multiple of AB that LN is of CD. Therefore GK, LN are equimultiples of AB, CD. Again, since HK is the same multiple of EB that MN is of FD, and KO is also the same multiple of EB that NP is of FD, therefore the sum HO is also the same multiple of EB that MP is of FD. [V. 2]  And, since, as AB is to BE, so is CD to DF, and of AB, CD equimultiples GK, LN have been taken, and of EB, FD equimultiples HO, MP, therefore, if GK is in excess of HO, LN is also in excess of MP, if equal, equal, and if less, less. Let GK be in excess of HO; then, if HK be subtracted from each, GH is also in excess of KO. But we saw that, if GK was in excess of HO, LN was also in excess of MP; therefore LN is also in excess of MP,  and, if MN be subtracted from each, LM is also in excess of NP; so that, if GH is in excess of KO, LM is also in excess of NP. Similarly we can prove that, if GH be equal to KO, LM will also be equal to NP, and if less, less. And GH, LM are equimultiples of AE, CF, while KO, NP are other, chance, equimultiples of EB, FD; therefore, as AE is to EB, so is CF to FD.
ai_proof_text:
5.17
**Statement:** If magnitudes be proportional componendo, they will also be proportional separando.

**Step 1.** Let AB, BE, CD, DF be magnitudes proportional componendo, so that AB : BE :: CD : DF. Since the ratio is taken componendo, the antecedent AB is the antecedent AE taken together with the consequent EB as one magnitude, and likewise CD is CF taken together with FD [D5.14]; thus AB is the sum of AE and EB, and CD is the sum of CF and FD. Since the four magnitudes are proportional, they have the same ratio [D5.6]. It is required to prove that they are also proportional separando, that is, that the excess AE is to EB as the excess CF is to FD [D5.15]: AE : EB :: CF : FD.

**Step 2.** Take any equimultiples whatever GH, HK, LM, MN of AE, EB, CF, FD respectively, each being the same multiple (say m times) of its magnitude, and any other equimultiples whatever KO, NP of EB, FD, each being the same multiple (say n times) of its magnitude, where m and n are arbitrary. Let GK denote the sum of GH and HK, LN the sum of LM and MN, HO the sum of HK and KO, and MP the sum of MN and NP.

**Step 3.** Since GH is the same multiple of AE that HK is of EB, the sum GK is the same multiple of the sum AB that GH is of AE [5.1]. In the same way, since LM is the same multiple of CF that MN is of FD, the sum LN is the same multiple of the sum CD that LM is of CF [5.1]. But GH and LM are equimultiples of AE and CF; therefore GK and LN are equimultiples of AB and CD.

**Step 4.** Since HK is the same multiple of EB that MN is of FD, and KO is also the same multiple of EB that NP is of FD, the sum HO is the same multiple of EB that the sum MP is of FD [5.2]. Therefore HO and MP are equimultiples of EB and FD.

**Step 5.** Now AB : BE :: CD : DF; GK, LN are equimultiples of the first and third, AB and CD; and HO, MP are equimultiples of the second and fourth, BE and DF. Therefore, by the definition of magnitudes in the same ratio [D5.5], if GK exceeds HO, LN exceeds MP; if GK is equal to HO, LN is equal to MP; and if GK falls short of HO, LN falls short of MP.

**Step 6.** GK is made up of GH together with HK, and HO is made up of KO together with the same HK. If GH is equal to KO, then, HK being added to each, GK is equal to HO [CN2]. If GH is greater than KO, then GH is made up of a magnitude equal to KO together with some excess; hence GK is made up of HO together with that excess, so that HO is a part of GK and GK is greater than HO [CN5]. If GH is less than KO, then in the same manner HO is made up of GK together with some excess, so that GK is a part of HO and GK is less than HO [CN5]. Now GH must be greater than, equal to, or less than KO, and these three mutually exclusive cases lead respectively to GK greater than, equal to, or less than HO, which likewise exclude one another; it therefore follows conversely that if GK is greater than HO, GH is greater than KO; if equal, equal; and if less, less. By the same argument applied to LN and MP with their common part MN: if LN is greater than MP, LM is greater than NP; if equal, equal; and if less, less.

**Step 7.** Combining Steps 5 and 6: if GH is greater than KO, then GK is greater than HO, hence LN is greater than MP, hence LM is greater than NP. If GH is equal to KO, then GK is equal to HO, LN is equal to MP, and LM is equal to NP. If GH is less than KO, then GK is less than HO, LN is less than MP, and LM is less than NP.

**Step 8.** But GH, LM are equimultiples of AE, CF, and KO, NP are other equimultiples of EB, FD, and the multiples m and n were taken at will. Therefore, whatever equimultiples be taken of AE and CF, and whatever equimultiples of EB and FD, the former alike exceed, are alike equal to, or alike fall short of the latter, taken in corresponding order. Therefore AE is to EB as CF is to FD [D5.5], that is, AE, EB, CF, FD are proportional [D5.6]; and since AE and CF are the excesses by which the antecedents AB and CD exceed the consequents EB and FD, the magnitudes AB, BE, CD, DF are proportional separando [D5.15]. Q.E.D.
